messages:
dave_acme: Hey team — our embeddings throughput just tanked for our overnight batch jobs. tokens/sec looks stable but vectors/sec dropped ~60% around 10:10 UTC. No client changes. We still get 200s but processing per-vector is much slower. headers we see: X-Tokens-Rate: 1250/s X-Vecs-Rate: 480/s (used to be ~2600/s). Can you check?

alice_support: Sorry about that — we're on it. Do you have a sample request and which model/variant you're using? Also any recent deploy time you noticed?

dave_acme: Sample: we POST /v1/embeddings with 512-d inputs, sending logical batches of 32 from our side. Model: text-embed-002-small (redwood-quant4). No client-side changes. Last successful run ~09:58 UTC.

ben_ml: quick question — did anyone rollout a batching config change? shrinking the batch_window or changing max_batch_size can collapse batching efficiency and kill vecs/sec even if tokens/sec looks ok.

carla_oncall: grabbing infra traces now. @infra-bot, show embed-pool-23 GPU queue depth / kvcache waits between 1719750000-1719755000 plz.

infra-bot: deploy record: batch-window-service v2.4 rolled at 1719749800 by infra-ci. Metrics (embed-pool-23): queue_depth avg=18 baseline -> spike to 85 at 1719754200; GPU_util avg=95% during spike; kvcache.lock_waits +230% around same time. Logs contain repeated: "fallback_to_cpu_quant: true" and "kvcache: lock held 120ms".

ben_ml: fallback_to_cpu_quant is a smoking gun — means some requests were routed off the optimized quantized path (bigger latency). tokens/sec steady because tokenization/prefix cache still serving, but vectorization path is bottlenecked (kv cache wait + smaller batches).

alice_support: Can we get a quick repro from our side? Dave — can you run this curl against prod and paste timings?

alice_support: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"text-embed-002-small","inputs": ["...512-d sample..."], "client_batch_hint":32}' 
```

ben_ml: I'll hit a canary with a probe that simulates many 1-5 item requests + bursty arrivals to exercise batching. Python quicktest: ```
from time import time
import requests
for _ in range(200):
  s=time(); r=requests.post(url, json={"model":"text-embed-002-small","inputs":[sample]} , headers=headers); print(time()-s)
```

ben_ml: Running probe against embed-pool-23 canary — result: average latency up 4.2x, vectors/sec down to ~420/s. Logs show small batch assembly and frequent cpu-quant fallback. Repro consistent with your report.

carla_oncall: Root cause hypothesis: v2.4 changed continuous_batching.window_ms from 20 -> 4 to reduce tail-latency for single-request workloads. Side effect: reduces effective batch sizes for embeddings, and combined with a quant-routing guard it forced some benches to fallback to a safe cpu-quant variant under contention. That explains high GPU_util + queue_depth spikes and kvcache lock waits.

alice_support: Proposed immediate mitigation: 1) rollback batch-window-service v2.4 for embed-pool-23 (rollback started), 2) increase continuous_batching.window_ms to 30ms for embed pools handling batch workloads, 3) enable kvcache backoff tuning to reduce lock storms, 4) temporary quota bump for affected customers while we stabilize.

infra-bot: rollback triggered: batch-window-service revert to v2.3 for embed-pool-23 at 1719754500. Canary now showing queue_depth back to ~16 and GPU_util 60-70%.

ben_ml: After rollback, probe shows vecs/sec recovered to ~2450/s on canary. CPU-fallback logs gone. Leaving a follow-up: add automated test that asserts vecs/sec/tokens/sec ratio for nightly loads and blocks batch-window rollouts that change window_ms by >5ms without perf test.

erin_product: We'll draft a customer-facing status blurb and an incident note summarizing timeline + workaround. @alice_support please confirm affected customers list so we can offer credits if SLA breached.

dave_acme: Thanks — appreciate the fast response. Can you share ETA for full rollout of the fix to our shard and the official postmortem?

alice_support: ETA: full rollback to all affected embed pools in the region by 1719755400 (rolling now). Postmortem and timeline will be posted to customers within 24 hours. We'll follow up with a temporary quota bump. :thumbsup:

ben_ml: Action items captured: - add vecs/sec regression test in canary pipeline - add guard on batch_window changes - investigate kvcache lock granularity and per-tenant backoff - schedule perf run for quant-routing under high queue_depth.

carla_oncall: Closing loop on oncall side: monitor for 2 hours post-rollback, escalate if queue_depth >30 or GPU_util >85%.

dave_acme: Confirmed our jobs are back to expected throughput. Thanks all.

alice_support: Closing thread, will attach runbook updates to the support ticket.
